groups.defect: Google CalendarService persists the zod safeParse wrapper {success, data} returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key instead of the parsed data, which corrupts the credential after the first refresh.
groups.rationale: All six point to the same lines in googlecalendar CalendarService and describe the same unwrap-.data defect.

groups.defect: zoho-bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint gets the wrong calcomUserId.
groups.rationale: Same call site, same defect, same fix.

groups.defect: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers (google res.data, hubspot, zoho .data.error, lark, webex) expect provider-specific shapes, so token refresh breaks.
groups.rationale: Three suggestions report it at the helper and one at the Google consumer. The defect is the same and is fixed by normalizing the helper's return value.

groups.defect: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys collapse to "[object Object]", so fields other than access_token are stripped. The literal "refresh_token" placeholder is then injected, applied even when sharing is off, and persisted over real refresh tokens.
groups.rationale: Members overlap on the schema-key collapse and the placeholder injection in parseRefreshTokenResponse, forming one chain.

groups.defect: The webhook's non-atomic findFirst→create can create duplicate credentials. It also lacks a method check, does not handle Zod or JSON parse errors, and does not validate the shape of the decrypted keys.
groups.rationale: Both report the findFirst/create race in app-credential.ts. s_bc9d8085 adds extra robustness defects.

groups.defect: Salesforce getClient eagerly refreshes the token on every instantiation, adding a network call and a hard failure point. It also uses the stale token for the connection, requires scope in the schema and checks statusText instead of response.ok.
groups.rationale: Both flag the unconditional eager refresh on every instantiation in the same lines, and each adds a different extra defect.
